title: Accurate and Convenient Energy Measurements for GPUs: A Detailed Study of NVIDIA GPU's Built-In Power Sensor
problem: NVIDIA GPUs' built-in power sensor has undocumented mechanisms and severe accuracy issues—for example, only 25% of runtime is sampled on A100 and H100 GPUs, causing drastic under/overestimation of energy consumption.
motivation: Accurate GPU power measurement is critical for understanding and improving energy efficiency of HPC systems, as power consumption has become a major bottleneck for further scaling.
method: Empirical evaluation of over 70 different GPUs across 12 architectural generations to characterize nvidia-smi power readings and identify accuracy problems. Analysis of sampling rates and measurement mechanisms revealed fundamental issues. Proposed and validated mitigations that reduce average energy measurement error by 35%.
key_novelty: First systematic characterization of NVIDIA's built-in power sensor across multiple GPU generations, identifying fundamental sampling and measurement accuracy issues with concrete mitigation strategies.
contributions: Detailed empirical characterization of nvidia-smi power sensor across 70+ GPUs and 12 architectural generations
Identification of critical accuracy problems including partial runtime sampling (25% on A100/H100 and similar issues across generations)
Proposed mitigations reducing average energy measurement error by 35%
Clarification of previously undocumented internal mechanisms of NVIDIA GPU power sensors

metrics.accuracy: 35% average error reduction in energy measurement
metrics.other: sampling rate characterization and measurement deviation analysis

primary_theme: GPU power sensor characterization and accuracy
